Status: blocked: needs an owner decision on the language of letters sent to brokers, and a native and legal read
Vendor: codex
Agent: i18n (Amara Okoye)
Owner contact: Morgan Reyes (check-ins via CODEX_TO_CLAUDE.md)
Kind: i18n
Epic: E10 (docs/vendor/EPICS.md)
Target release: 0.4
Source: in-house 0.4 epic batch 2026-11-09 (in-house offline until about Nov 14; vendors keep working the queue in epic order)
Worktree: none until unblocked (then `.vendor-wt/wo-417` on `vendor/wo-417` from main)
Tracker: issue pending (in-house syncs freemyid-pm)

## Goal
For each letter template in `letters.TEMPLATES` (`engine/letters.py:22-23`: generic, California, other state, follow-up, formal demand, postal letter, phone script, value removal) write a short Spanish explainer in the glossary's register: what the letter asks for, what it cites (only when the matrix says the citation is verified, `law_matrix.py:62-67`), when it is sent, and what the person does with it. Draft only, each paragraph marked "draft for native and legal review".

## Blocked: what in-house must provide first
The owner must decide whether letters to US brokers stay in English with a Spanish explanation shown next to them (this WO's assumption), or are sent in Spanish too. Brokers' privacy teams read English and a Spanish-only request may not be handled, so the recommendation is: letters stay English, the app explains them in Spanish. In-house must confirm that decision in a GO message, and name who does the native-speaker and legal review of the Spanish text before anything ships. Until then no Spanish sentence about a legal request should be drafted.

Not startable by a vendor. In-house unblocks it by changing the status line and posting a GO.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)
1. One section per template, each under 120 words, usted register, terms from `GLOSSARY_ES.md` only (unknown terms are added there first, "needs native review").
2. States clearly that the letter itself is in English and why; never says the request is guaranteed or that the site must obey, and never gives legal advice beyond what the letter says.
3. Any statute named matches the verified matrix entry (`brokers/state_law_deletion_matrix.yaml`) and carries its source URL from that file; anything unverified says "not sure" in English in a note for the reviewer.
4. A header marks the whole file as a draft, with the review owner left blank for in-house to fill.
5. Every claim about when a letter is sent cites file:line (`engine/outbox.py`, `engine/runner.py`).
6. No "garantía", "borrar para siempre", "100%" or "seguro" as promises.

Docs/tests-only work in Codex's lane. Fake people only (Jane Q Testperson, Springfield IL), offline, Windows-safe paths. Check `tests/codex/`, `tests/grok/` and in-house `tests/test_*.py` first; don't duplicate a guard. Every claim cites file:line from main at the time of writing; re-check them.
